title: Come, Spirit of God
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: The mission is impossible in our own strength. With the Spirit, it is inevitable. The gospel is designed to spread through the weakest vessels.
exhortation: This is the end of Peter's sermon right after Pentecost, the first Spirit-filled sermon of the new covenant. Doesn't it make your heart surge with joy? It does mine, to hear the power of the Spirit pouring out through Peter as he proclaims Jesus.

The first thing that struck me is that Jesus was given the Spirit to accomplish his mission, and then he turned and gave that same inheritance to us. That's what he told the apostles before he left: don't lose heart, because it is better that I go. The Spirit is coming. His presence is poured out on his people.

And I love Peter's promise: "The promise is for you and for your children and for all who are far off." This limitless, powerful gospel will pour out to everyone, to your children and your children's children. And we are called to this mission.

Let's be honest: the mission is impossible in our own strength. If it depends on our willpower, our rhetoric and our strategies, on having exactly the right thing to say at exactly the right moment, it won't work. Like Jonathan said yesterday about his conversation in the store: if it depended on him finding the perfect words, it wouldn't succeed. In fact, the gospel is designed to spread through the weakest vessels. That's us.

Peter wasn't a world-famous apostle yet. He was a former fisherman who was probably getting the side-eye from a crowd that thought he seemed a little loony. But filled with the Holy Spirit, he became bold Peter, eyes fixed on Christ alone, willing to give a hard word to his brothers who needed to hear it. And look at the response. We became Christians by the power of the Holy Spirit, and that is how new Christians will come to Christ: not by our cleverness, but by our obedience in the power of the Spirit.
prayer: How we need you, Lord. We can do nothing except by the power of your Spirit. Let us humbly walk in the ways you have set before us, and obey with full faith that you are good and faithful and that your work is finished. In our own strength this is impossible. With your Spirit, it is inevitable.

What a glorious truth that the power in us is greater than the power in the world. So often we're fearful or discouraged because we compare our power to the world's. That isn't the comparison. It is our almighty, unstoppable God who is with us, against a finite world that will be defeated. Give us eyes to see the harvest and hearts of compassion to share your word, remembering that we were once lost and your enemies when you showed us grace and sent someone to tell us the gospel. May we be those people to a lost and dying world. In Jesus' name, amen.
